caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 106 of 2004.
lawyer:
AKM Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record---For the Petitioner. 
Not represented---The Respondent.
parties:
Chitta Ranjan Das alias Chitta Ranjan Sinha ------ Petitioner
vs
Shashi Mohan Das ------ Respondent
full_judgment: 2. That the case of the prosecution is that complainant Shashi Mohan Das filed a complaint in the Court of Senior Special Judge, Sunamganj on 21-7-1997 alleging, inter alia, that he along with his brother Hari Mohan are owners of 3.17 acre of land of Dag No. 1914 appertaining to Khatian No. 70 of Mouza Mirjapur within PS Bulla of District Sunamganj. Accused Chitta Ranjan Sinha made a forged document being Deed No. 8258 dated 18-10-1960 in which accused's father was shown as buyer and complainant's father was shown as seller of the said plot. The accused applied to the Thana Revenue Officer for mutation who instructed accused No. 2 Harupada Roy, Tahsilder to give report and accused No. 2 gave false report that petitioner's father Shyam Lal Das was shown to be alive though he died long ago and accused Ershad Ali, Process Server gave a report that the process was duly served and thereby accused No. 1 committed an offence under sections 467/471 of the Penal Code and accused Nos. 2 and 3 being public servants committed an offence under sections 467/109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, mutation of the said land in the name of the father of accused No. 1 was duly made in Mutation Case No. 409 of 1996-1997. The complainant filed an appeal being Appeal No. 6 of1997 in the Court of ADC (Revenue), Sunamganj and ADC (Revenue) cancelled the aforesaid mutation by his order dated 31-6-1997. Meanwhile, accused No. 1 filed a Title Suit No. 3 of 1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sulla on 29-5-1997 for correction of records. That upon receiving the aforesaid complaint and hearing the Advocate the Special Case No. 4 of 1997 was registered in the Court of Senior Special Judge, Sunamganj and on the order of the Court Bureau of Anti-Corruption conducted enquiry and reported about genuineness of the allegation and the Court having found prima facie case against them under sections 419/420/467/468/471/ 109 and under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 took cognizance by the order No. 20 dated 17-10-1999.
